{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6kBb2HH6mGcMU8fwov","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MdqDEzWoBVgaU1X1npNn9G","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-005/2026-07-24T151330Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why production hits the public Base RPC\n\n## The exact chain\n\n**1. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is a build-time constant, not a runtime read.**\nIn Next.js, `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` is not looked up at runtime.\nWebpack's DefinePlugin does a **textual substitution at `next build` time**:\nevery occurrence of `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in the bundle is\nreplaced with the string literal that was present in the *build*\nenvironment. After that, the value is frozen into the JS chunks. There is\nno `process.env` object in the browser to consult later.\n\n**2. Dev machines vs. the production build see different environments.**\nOn a developer machine, `.env.local` (or the shell) has\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL=<paid RPC>`, so at build/dev time it is inlined as the\npaid URL — hence no 429s locally.\n\nThe production artifact is a **static Next.js build on generic hosting**.\nIf the CI/build step that ran `next build` did **not** have\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` set in its environment, then `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL`\nevaluates to `undefined` and gets inlined as `undefined`. Setting the var\nin the *host's* runtime env does nothing — the value was already baked in\nat build time. This is the root misconception: people set it on the server\nwhere the site is served, not in the environment where it was compiled.\n\n**3. `undefined` override → the transport falls through to the public RPC.**\nIn `scaffold.config.ts`:\n```ts\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL }\n```\nIn production this becomes `{ [base.id]: undefined }`.\n\nIn `wagmiConfig.tsx` the client builder does:\n```ts\nlet rpcFallbacks = [http()];                     // http() with NO url = chain's default *public* RPC\nconst rpcOverrideUrl = scaffoldConfig.rpcOverrides?.[chain.id];\nif (rpcOverrideUrl) {\n  rpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\n} else {\n  // no override → try Alchemy, else keep [http()]\n  ...\n}\ntransport: fallback(rpcFallbacks)\n```\n`rpcOverrideUrl` is `undefined` → falsy → the `if` is skipped. With no\nAlchemy key configured (or the default shared key), `rpcFallbacks` stays\n`[http()]`. **`http()` with no argument resolves to the chain's built-in\ndefault RPC — for Base that's `mainnet.base.org`.** Every production request\ntherefore lands on the public endpoint and gets rate-limited (429).\n\nSo: unset build-time env var → `undefined` override → `else` branch →\nbare `http()` → public Base RPC → 429s.\n\n## The one operational check that settles whether the fix is real\n\n**Grep the actually-deployed JS bundle (or watch the production Network tab)\nfor the RPC hostname.** Because the value is baked in at build time, the only\nproof is in the shipped artifact, not in any server config screen:\n\n- Confirm the paid RPC URL string appears in the deployed `_next/static/*.js`\n  chunks, and that `mainnet.base.org` is **not** the endpoint the JSON-RPC\n  `POST`s go to.\n- Equivalently, open the live site, DevTools → Network, and verify the\n  `eth_*` POST requests target the paid host.\n\nCorollary this check enforces: the fix is to set `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in the\n**build/CI environment and re-run `next build`**, then redeploy. Setting it as\na runtime env var on the host changes nothing for a static export.\n\n## The second, transport-level trap (persists even after the env var is fixed)\n\nIn `packages/nextjs/services/web3/wagmiConfig.tsx`, once the override is\npresent the code builds:\n```ts\nrpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\ntransport: fallback(rpcFallbacks)\n```\nThe **bare `http()` public RPC is still the second entry in the `fallback`\nlist.** wagmi/viem's `fallback` transport uses the first healthy transport\nbut **spills over to the next one on any error, timeout, or 429** from the\npaid endpoint. Under production load, a single transient failure (or the\npaid provider's own rate limit / a slow response) silently routes that\nrequest to `mainnet.base.org` — which then gets rate-limited too. So a\nsubset of requests keeps hitting the public RPC even though the primary is\nnow the paid one, and it's intermittent/hard to spot.\n\n**Fix for the trap:** don't keep the unauthenticated `http()` as the fallback\nfor a paid setup — either use `fallback([http(rpcOverrideUrl)])` (override\nonly), or make the second entry a *second authenticated* endpoint, so no\nfailure path leads to a public RPC.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":419,"cache_read_input_tokens":21204,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":419},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6c62d171-7399-4ae2-a212-967c7953ffcb","uuid":"01116e7d-aed7-420e-86ca-b26b3c07a4bb","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:14:44.751Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6kAr7zSyB8pHPV9GVe"}

After that, the value is frozen into the JS chunks. There is\nno `process.env` object in the browser to consult later.\n\n**2. Dev machines vs. the production build see different environments.**\nOn a developer machine, `.env.local` (or the shell) has\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL=<paid RPC>`, so at build/dev time it is inlined as the\npaid URL — hence no 429s locally.\n\nThe production artifact is a **static Next.js build on generic hosting**.\nIf the CI/build step that ran `next build` did **not** have\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` set in its environment, then `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL`\nevaluates to `undefined` and gets inlined as `undefined`. Setting the var\nin the *host's* runtime env does nothing — the value was already baked in\nat build time. This is the root misconception: people set it on the server\nwhere the site is served, not in the environment where it was compiled.\n\n**3. `undefined` override → the transport falls through to the public RPC.**\nIn `scaffold.config.ts`:\n```ts\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL }\n```\nIn production this becomes `{ [base.id]: undefined }`.\n\nIn `wagmiConfig.tsx` the client builder does:\n```ts\nlet rpcFallbacks = [http()];                     // http() with NO url = chain's default *public* RPC\nconst rpcOverrideUrl = scaffoldConfig.rpcOverrides?.[chain.id];\nif (rpcOverrideUrl) {\n  rpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\n} else {\n  // no override → try Alchemy, else keep [http()]\n  ...\n}\ntransport: fallback(rpcFallbacks)\n```\n`rpcOverrideUrl` is `undefined` → falsy → the `if` is skipped. With no\nAlchemy key configured (or the default shared key), `rpcFallbacks` stays\n`[http()]`. **`http()` with no argument resolves to the chain's built-in\ndefault RPC — for Base that's `mainnet.base.org`.** Every production request\ntherefore lands on the public endpoint and gets rate-limited (429).\n\nSo: unset build-time env var → `undefined` override → `else` branch →\nbare `http()` → public Base RPC → 429s.\n\n## The one operational check that settles whether the fix is real\n\n**Grep the actually-deployed JS bundle (or watch the production Network tab)\nfor the RPC hostname.** Because the value is baked in at build time, the only\nproof is in the shipped artifact, not in any server config screen:\n\n- Confirm the paid RPC URL string appears in the deployed `_next/static/*.js`\n  chunks, and that `mainnet.base.org` is **not** the endpoint the JSON-RPC\n  `POST`s go to.\n- Equivalently, open the live site, DevTools → Network, and verify the\n  `eth_*` POST requests target the paid host.\n\nCorollary this check enforces: the fix is to set `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in the\n**build/CI environment and re-run `next build`**, then redeploy. Setting it as\na runtime env var on the host changes nothing for a static export.\n\n## The second, transport-level trap (persists even after the env var is fixed)\n\nIn `packages/nextjs/services/web3/wagmiConfig.tsx`, once the override is\npresent the code builds:\n```ts\nrpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];\ntransport: fallback(rpcFallbacks)\n```\nThe **bare `http()` public RPC is still the second entry in the `fallback`\nlist.** wagmi/viem's `fallback` transport uses the first healthy transport\nbut **spills over to the next one on any error, timeout, or 429** from the\npaid endpoint. Under production load, a single transient failure (or the\npaid provider's own rate limit / a slow response) silently routes that\nrequest to `mainnet.base.org` — which then gets rate-limited too. So a\nsubset of requests keeps hitting the public RPC even though the primary is\nnow the paid one, and it's intermittent/hard to spot.\n\n**Fix for the trap:** don't keep the unauthenticated `http()` as the fallback\nfor a paid setup — either use `fallback([http(rpcOverrideUrl)])` (override\nonly), or make the second entry a *second authenticated* endpoint, so no\nfailure path leads to a public RPC.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
